ingredients.cook_qty: 2 tbsp chopped + a little to finish

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.

Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, changing the water until it runs clear, then drain it. Put the rice in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave the lid on until the curry is ready.

In a large bowl, combine the turkey, egg, 2 tbsp chopped chives, the coriander, 3 tbsp of the flour, 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Mix with your hands until it is smooth and no streaks of egg are left. Stop there. Mixing longer makes the koftas dense.
With damp hands, roll the mixture into 16 balls, about the size of a golf ball. Place them on the baking sheet, leaving a little space between them, and brush them with 1 tbsp of the oil.

Bake for 14 minutes, until they are browned and cooked through. You're cooking them to 165°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
While they bake, chop the bell pepper. Grate the ginger and mince the garlic.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds. They will pop after about 30 seconds, so stand back a little.
Add the bell pepper and cook for 3 minutes, until it softens. Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Stir in the remaining 1 tbsp flour and the curry powder. Cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the curry leaves. Stir until smooth, then simmer for 5 minutes, until the sauce has thickened.
Add the spinach by the handful and stir for 1 minute, until it has wilted.
Add the koftas to the sauce, spoon the sauce over them, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice and scatter a little chopped chive on top.
method_notes: Becky Excell's turkey kofta curry (Gluten Free Cuppa Tea, 4.96 from 23) is the lead: turkey thigh mixed with egg, coriander and gluten-free flour, baked, then added to a mustard seed, red pepper and curry powder coconut sauce with spinach. The other pages (Discover Great Veg, easyFood, The Curry Theory) have no usable ratings. The lead stirs yogurt in at the end, which is left out to keep this dairy-free; the chili flakes are left out to keep it mild, and the garlic oil is plain oil with fresh garlic. The list's line says a tomato curry, but the lead is a coconut curry with no tomato, so this follows the lead.
